Its three foreign subsidiaries provide ER&D services customised to the specific needs of every individual customer.

risks.note: Management explicitly flags that a potential slowdown in the North American or European economies could exert a dampening effect on the Company's overall growth trajectory. TAAL Tech's customers sit in North America, Europe and APAC, so the revenue base is directly exposed to those two economies' capital and engineering-spend cycles.
risks.risk: Developed-market demand concentration - North America and Europe

risks.note: Stated verbatim: although the macro-outlook for growth in the ER&D space remains positive, 'global geopolitical and economic risks persist'. This is the framing risk management places around an otherwise positive outlook.

Management states it is 'yet to be able to assess the full impact of AI on the engineering services sector' and will assess it as it goes along. For a labour-based ER&D services provider this is an unquantified structural risk to the pricing and effort-based revenue model; the stated response is to stay abreast of industry trends and adopt the technology to improve efficiencies.
risks.risk: AI disruption of the engineering services model - impact not yet assessable

risks.note: A structural concentration disclosure not labelled as a risk: 'more than seventy percent of our business comes from customers who have been with us more than ten years'. Strategy is explicitly to grow 'around key strategic customers'. The relationship depth is presented as a strength, but it also means the majority of revenue rests on a small set of long-standing accounts.
risks.risk: Customer concentration / dependence on long-tenured key accounts

risks.note: The MD&A states 'Human Resource Management is critical to the successful functioning of our Company' and that it is the Company's endeavour to nurture a high-performance culture focused on efficiency, innovation and talent growth. Capability and headcount are the delivery capacity of an asset-light services firm. Note: no attrition rate, headcount or utilisation figure is disclosed in the routed text.
risks.risk: Talent dependence in a people-based ER&D business

risks.note: All three subsidiaries are foreign (USA, Switzerland, UK) and revenue is earned from North America, Europe and APAC customers; the Board's Report notes that foreign exchange earnings and outgo particulars are given as Annexure A. The FX and multi-jurisdiction exposure is structural, though the Company does not itself label it a risk in the routed text.
risks.risk: Cross-border / foreign-currency and multi-jurisdiction operating exposure

risks.note: TAAL Enterprises Limited merged with its wholly owned subsidiary TAAL Tech India Private Limited during the year and the merged entity was renamed TAAL Tech Limited to retain brand recognition. Management states the merger was 'effected smoothly without any interruption to business', so this is a disclosed-and-mitigated item rather than an open risk, but it changes the reporting entity and the comparability of the corporate history.
risks.risk: Execution/integration risk around the merger and the change of corporate identity

risks.note: M/s. V P Thacker & Co. were re-appointed as Statutory Auditors at the 11th AGM for five years till the 16th AGM, but during the year that firm merged with M/s. Lodha & Bhatt, creating a casual vacancy; the Board appointed M/s. TLB & Co. on February 10, 2026 to hold office until the conclusion of the 12th AGM. Mitigants disclosed: the statutory audit report carries an unmodified opinion with no qualification, reservation, adverse remark or disclaimer; the Secretarial Audit Report likewise carries no qualification; and neither auditor reported any instance of fraud under Section 143(12) during the year.
risks.risk: Statutory auditor discontinuity - casual vacancy filled mid-year
